verdicts.evidence: Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes.
verdicts.reason: The agent disclosed the recording in the opening turn, within the first minute.

verdicts.evidence: Before I go into any of your details or a quote, can I just confirm your full name and date of birth please?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked for full name and date of birth before discussing details or a quote, and confirmed them at 00:41.

verdicts.evidence: So to make sure we look at the right thing for you, can you tell me a bit about your situation and why you're thinking about life cover?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked about the customer's circumstances and reasons before recommending any cover amount.

verdicts.evidence: Acme Life Cover lets you choose a cover amount anywhere from fifty thousand up to one million dollars
verdicts.reason: The cover range, stepped premiums, terminal illness benefit, two-year pre-existing condition exclusion and 30-day free-look all match the product facts. The quoted monthly premiums are not in the facts and are not a contradiction.

verdicts.evidence: There's no rush on our side, the cover's available whenever you're ready.
verdicts.reason: The agent told the customer the decision was theirs and used no false urgency, and offered a call back and an email summary.

verdicts.evidence: If you're happy with two fifty, I can take you through the application questions now, it takes about fifteen minutes.
verdicts.reason: No sale was completed; the customer said I won't decide today.

verdicts.evidence: If you wanted, we could also look at a lower cover amount, say one fifty thousand, which would bring the starting premium down to about one hundred and twelve a month.
verdicts.reason: The customer disclosed a recent stroke, muddled words, losing track and foggy thinking, and said it was a lot at once. The agent did not slow down or check understanding, and kept adding options and figures. It did offer an email and a call back and suggested going through it with his wife, but that was not enough.
Doesn't apply in the NZ market.
